The 7-day entry-date window (2026-11-05 → 2026-11-12) returned one arthroscopic wrist citation across the six journals — the Hand Clinics review of arthroscopic management of volar and dorsal wrist ganglia from Western University and Emory, with Eric Wagner as corresponding author (PMID 43003551, included below and labelled from our own group). The remaining twelve therefore come from the backfill queue carried forward on 2026-11-07: the held JHS European distal radius update was read and excluded (see below), the three unscreened 2022-pool citations and the fifteen unscreened 2021-pool citations were all screened, and twelve qualified. None of those twelve is a new publication — each is flagged with its original publication date below. The standing non-arthroscopic keyword screen was run (per the vocabulary-blindspot rule) across all nine wrist-related citations entering the six journals between 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-12. The thread running through this week. The fovea, and what to do when the hook test is all you have. Restricted to wrist arthroscopic techniques and closely related work. Author line = first & senior author; corresponding-author institution listed per article. 13 articles. A dry live week, filled entirely from the queue. The 7-day entry-date window (2026-10-02 → 2026-10-11) returned one citation — the Journal of Hand Surgery dermal-matrix interposition series (PMID 42825736), which was already covered in the 2026-10-03 digest. The window was widened: the 30-day entry-date sweep returned seven and a 90-day publication-date sweep returned 16, and every one of them reconciles against PMIDs already covered in this track. Widening therefore yields nothing new, so this week draws on the backfill queue carried forward since 2026-09-22: thirteen older arthroscopic papers (2020–2023) that had been screened, judged qualifying, and held for a dry week. None of these thirteen is a new publication — each is flagged with its original publication date below. The standing non-arthroscopic keyword screen was run (per the vocabulary-blindspot rule) across all 39 citations entering these six journals in the last 7 days. One wrist-adjacent item without an arthroscopy-stem term was pulled and read: the Journal of Hand Surgery review on the evolution of total trapeziometacarpal arthroplasty toward dual-mobility systems (PMID 42841833) — an open implant review with no arthroscopic content, so it is not counted. The rest of the week was JBJS spine, arthroplasty, and global-orthopaedics content and commentaries (including a commentary on AI fracture detection in distal radial fractures), Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery body-contouring and education papers, and a JHS review on pregnant and postpartum patients. The thread running through this week. Ulnar-sided wrist pain, and the arthroscopic toolkit for it. Hand Clinics' 2021 ulnar-wrist issue supplies four reviews — TFCC repair and reconstruction, TFCC tears in children, lunotriquetral tears, and ulnocarpal impaction — and the Kakar–Burnier group adds three papers on dry wrist arthroscopy, the technique that makes bony and ligament work through the scope practical. Around those sit a cadaveric safety study of a volar distal radioulnar portal, a sobering case series of thermal-wand injuries, and four papers on the most common thing anyone scopes in the wrist: the ganglion. item.title: Wrist Arthroscopy — 2026-10-03
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Wrist Arthroscopy Literature Digest — 2026-10-03 Pulled from PubMed across the six target journals — JBJS Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Wrist Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics. Restricted to wrist arthroscopic techniques and closely related work. Author line = first & senior author; corresponding-author institution listed per article. 10 articles. A thin live week, filled from the queue. The 7-day entry-date window (2026-09-26 → 2026-10-04) returned one qualifying citation — a Journal of Hand Surgery case series on arthroscopic dermal-matrix interposition for wrist chondral lesions. Because that falls well short of the ~5-paper floor, the window was widened. The 30-day entry-date sweep returned seven, and the six beyond this week's paper were all covered in the 2026-09-26 digest; a 90-day publication-date sweep returned 16, every one of which reconciled against PMIDs already covered in this track. Widening the recent window therefore yields nothing new, so this week draws on the backfill queue carried forward since 2026-09-22: nine older arthroscopic papers (2020–2021) that had been screened, judged qualifying, and held for exactly this kind of dry week. These nine are not new publications — they are flagged with their original publication dates below. The standing non-arthroscopic keyword screen was run (per the vocabulary-blindspot rule) across all 57 citations entering these six journals in the last 7 days. One wrist item without any arthroscopy-stem term was pulled and read: the Hand Clinics case report on salvage of the distal radioulnar joint after failed fixation (PMID 42816022), which ends in a Scheker prosthesis — open, implant-based work with no arthroscopic content, so it is not counted. The rest of the week was the November Hand Clinics upper-limb reconstruction issue, brachial plexus and metacarpal papers, and the October Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery discussions and replies. The thread running through this week. Joint preservation, done through the scope, in places where the default answer has been open surgery or a fusion. A dermal-matrix interposition for Outerbridge IV chondral lesions that keeps 17 wrists out of a salvage procedure at two years; a debridement and arthrolysis for Lichtman III–IV Kienböck that holds at five years despite radiographic progression; thermal shrinkage for palmar midcarpal instability that is still working at twelve years; and electrothermal treatment of low-grade scapholunate tears with 90% back to pre-injury function at seven. None of these is a large or controlled series. Together they make the case that "minimal" arthroscopic procedures earn more durable results than their reputation suggests. From our own group: no Wagner-authored paper appeared this week. Journals with no qualifying articles: JBJS Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, and Hand Clinics. The single live paper is from J Hand Surg Am; the backfill papers are from J Wrist Surg (8) and J Hand Surg Eur Vol (1). ---

item.title: Wrist Arthroscopy — 2026-09-26
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Wrist Arthroscopy Literature Digest — 2026-09-26 Pulled from PubMed across the six target journals — JBJS Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Wrist Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics. Restricted to wrist arthroscopic techniques and closely related work. Author line = first & senior author; corresponding-author institution listed per article. 6 articles. A live week, and a genuinely good one. After last week's backfill digest, the 7-day entry-date window (2026-09-19 → 2026-09-27) returned six citations, all six new and all six qualifying — the entire October 2026 issue of the Journal of Wrist Surgery landed at once. No window-widening was needed. For completeness the 30-day entry-date sweep returned the same six, and a 90-day publication-date sweep returned 10, every one of which reconciled against PMIDs already covered in this track or the wrist-arthroplasty track. The standing non-arthroscopic keyword screen was run (per the vocabulary-blindspot rule) across all 67 citations entering these six journals in the last 14 days. Six wrist papers without any arthroscop term were pulled and read: scaphoid nonunion fixation with headless compression screws (42788187), scaffold fixation of multifragmented intra-articular distal radius fractures (42788181), dorsal lunate dislocation systematic review (42787919), revision rates after scapholunate repair/reconstruction in PearlDiver (42787912), scaphoid morphology after nonunion fixation (42788150), and delayed DRUJ dysfunction after paediatric forearm fractures (42788182). None contains arthroscopic technique content — all are open, radiographic, or administrative-database work — so none is counted. The SL revision-rate database study (1,320 patients, 5-year follow-up) is the one worth knowing about as background for the reconstruction papers below, and it is flagged here rather than in the digest proper. The thread running through this week. Two independent Australian series arrive at the same conclusion from different directions: dorsal-ulnar TFCC pathology does not travel alone. In the Sydney dorsal-TFCC cohort, 55% had concurrent scapholunate instability; in the Perth ECU series, six of seven had a concurrent dorsal peripheral TFCC tear or SL instability requiring arthroscopic repair at the same sitting. Both groups make the same practical argument — the ulnar-sided wrist that hurts on pronosupination is usually a multi-structure injury, and a scope that only looks where the MRI pointed will under-call it. The MRI numbers in the first paper are the ones that will stick with you: dorsal TFCC tears correctly identified in 14%, and the TFCC read as entirely normal in 48%. From our own group: no Wagner-authored paper appeared this week. Journals with no qualifying articles: JBJS Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics. The arthroscopy keyword search returned nothing new — again, and this time it is not a search failure. The 14-day edat window (2026-08-25 → 2026-09-08) returned zero citations. A 3.5-year arthroscopall sweep across all six journals returned 244 citations and surfaced exactly one uncovered wrist-journal item. This is what the exhausted-backfill state actually looks like: the six journals genuinely did not publish a new wrist-arthroscopy paper in this window. So the week was rebuilt two other ways. First, the standing non-arthroscopic journal screen (six journals, 30-day entry date, wrist/carpal topic terms, no arthroscop requirement) returned 20 citations — the sweep that caught the Washington University foveal repair paper a fortnight ago. Part A is arthroscopic or directly arthroscopy-relevant — the constructs, the portals, the biomechanics of the operations we perform through a scope. Part B is the closely related non-arthroscopic literature in the in-scope conditions (scaphoid nonunion, Kienböck, DRUJ instability, SLAC/SNAC, CMC arthritis), included because it changes the decisions around the arthroscopic ones, and flagged as non-arthroscopic throughout so nothing here is mistaken for scope work.
